matches.route: Capsaicin / local sensory defunctionalization and analgesia
matches.disposition: Retain symptom-specific local analgesia reserve; no current MVA muscle or BUBR1-restoration nomination
matches.rationale: Local capsaicin pretreatment reduced spontaneous foot-lift duration and mechanical/heat hypersensitivity in a rat incision model, with local sensory denervation. The printed overall frequency P=.059 is not significant; heat responses exceed baseline for several days, so this is sensory suppression rather than demonstrated regeneration. Bub1b is an injury-versus-sham RNA decrease; no gene-specific drug response or BUBR1 protein/segregation assay is supplied. Figure 2 overlap labels conflict with the claimed global transcript reversal. A separate mouse primary is abstract-only; its fully read correction adds funding, not altered experimental results. Preserve measured analgesia without transferring it to dietary intake, muscle output or MVA rescue.
matches.evidence_scope: Actual symptom or biomarker benefits retained; source assay, formulation and disease limits distinguished.

source_start.reading_limit: Relevant current ledger identity only; earlier capsaicin evidence not newly qualified.

preparation.placebo: Maltodextrin, excipients and red dye; amounts unreported
preparation.packaging: Non-involved researcher at Life Pro Nutrition industries, Madrid; identical appearance/color/taste claimed
preparation.administration: One assigned condition per week, capsule orally with water under supervision 45 min before the first weekly exercise; no 24-hour redose described.
preparation.batch_purity_assay: Not established. Introduction 98% composition is cited background, not a verified trial-batch assay.
preparation.medicine_or_pediatric_approval: Not established; cited EFSA opinion not independently qualified.

design.randomizer: Third-party Research Randomizer assignment two weeks before the study.
design.period_schedule: One condition weekly, first exercise session plus a 24-hour assessment.
design.washout: Weekly spacing reported; no explicitly validated pharmacological washout, measured clearance, or previous-treatment carryover model.
design.blinding: Codes 1–3; not unblinded until independent researcher completed analyses; success not assessed.
design.pretesting: Initial anthropometry, 1RM, load–velocity and familiarization two weeks before; each period pre-exercise measurements followed the capsule/warm-up schedule.
design.diet_activity: Maintain diet; avoid stimulants/ergogenic aids and strenuous training before testing; dietary adherence not directly recorded.

exercise.main_protocol: 3 sets × 8 repetitions at 70% 1RM, 2-min rest; load adjusted daily from warm-up and load–velocity relationship.

analysis.power_basis: Prior squat total volume; alpha .05, power .80, effect size .60, minimum 21 participants.
analysis.model: Repeated-measures condition × time ANOVA with Bonferroni pairwise tests; one-way ANOVA for total volume/individual repetitions; Greenhouse–Geisser where Mauchly test significant.
analysis.order_analysis: Supplement Tables S1–S3 group by week; invalid P values and P=.05 prevent a blanket no-order-effect claim; not proof of no carryover.

CMJ.pairwise_time_scope: Not explicitly assigned to a specific post-exercise time in Results; no verified 24-hour advantage.

outcomes.velocity_pairwise_limit: Combined Results velocity paragraph reports Bonferroni condition comparisons P=.06–.07; no complete outcome-by-pair listing; omnibus positives are not substituted for pairwise benefit.
outcomes.individual_repetitions_abstract: Comparator assignment reversed: HD>LD P=.01; HD>PLA P=.004–.008.

isometric.interpretation: Tests were performed; controlled results were nonpositive. MIF percent/scale and RFD time-label issues remain unresolved.

EMG.interpretation: No significant condition or interaction effects; time effects are not treatment effects. No established neural mediation.

outcomes.force_2point5_percent_discussion: Cited association from another relationship, not a measured trial treatment effect on force.

## Accepted source review and integration proposal provenance

Independent review accepted this source-bounded qualification. The original producer object is preserved exactly inside the structured companion; its historical pending-review status is retained there. The Markdown has only the documented disposition-status replacement and this appended provenance section. Scientific findings and limitations are unchanged.

The source producer was `/root/quercetin_primary`; the independent source reviewer was `/root/maxepa_primary`. The latter also prepared this external proposal, reusing the same reading rather than supplying a third independent scientific review. Source-first findings were frozen before the reviewer opened producer conclusions; substantive concerns and timing clarification were discussed before the producer freeze. The review is independent with task context, not blinded. Producer and reviewer reading scopes remain separately recorded.

The proposed entry is an acute healthy-adult performance comparator. Exact phenylcapsaicin and aXivite name candidates are supported by the original Methods. Current saved catalog/FDA/SGC records have no matching name; NIH DSLD source group3951 has both names as synonyms under Capsaicin. Name relations do not establish chemical equivalence to ordinary capsaicin or a tested retail product. No main report, pitch, research-priority matrix, nominee or current count is changed by this external proposal. Root owns any later combined integration, identity joins and count reconciliation. HMB transplant is a separate accepted source and is excluded from this proposal.

Producer freeze: `328ac4fe55974e0cae76b5351f13a1abc5f481c55bd3c421efc74b7f86f4cc0a`. Independent-review freeze: `b4b99f9c2f17b5c682f0a2a7175e3db873107af50846877b2ae60e4eccd5874e`. Proposal baseline: clean `52de81f0299fd4573c56b49332eb9fb15327c43d`,280 assessments. Raw assets remain external; this portable export adds no primary-reading, biological-replication or efficacy credit.

proposed_decision.route: Phenylcapsaicin (aXivite study preparation) / acute healthy-adult mechanical-performance comparator
proposed_decision.disposition: Retain bounded acute jump and selected-repetition performance findings with measured nulls and reporting limitations; no MVA-efficacy or nominee promotion
proposed_decision.evidence_scope: Complete original scientific main and original supplement. The producer read main text and native pages 4 and 6–10 covering all outcome tables and figures; the independent source reviewer read all 11 native main pages and the complete supplement text and seven locally rendered pages. Source-first concerns were discussed before producer freeze, not blind convergence. No own registered protocol/SAP or participant data was recovered; later registry candidates are different studies. This proposal reuses those readings and adds no independent source-reading credit.
proposed_decision.rationale: A randomized, triple-blinded crossover study gave healthy trained young men 2.5 mg or 0.625 mg phenylcapsaicin (aXivite), or maltodextrin/excipient placebo, before a squat session. Twenty-five enrolled and two withdrew; outcome-specific analysis counts remain unclear. The main reports a CMJ condition-by-time interaction (Table 3 P=.01), with corrected high-dose comparisons above placebo and low dose (both P<.001), but their time-specific scope is not explicit. Selected repetition-velocity comparisons are positive; the abstract reverses the comparator assignments printed in Results. Omnibus condition tests for 60%-load velocity, mean within-set velocity and velocity loss were significant, but reported Bonferroni condition comparisons were not (P=.06–.07). Isometric force/RFD, EMG, total volume and best-velocity findings were nonpositive. These are measured functional outcomes without demonstrated maximum-1RM or 24-hour recovery benefit. Weekly scheduling does not prove absence of carryover. Supplemental tables contain invalid P values of 1.83, 2.89 and 1.57, a week P=.05, inconsistent labels and discrepant descriptives; these remain unrepaired. No adverse effects were reported, without systematic safety counts or injury-withdrawal attribution. Industry material support and adviser roles are disclosed. Exposure is nominal supervised study dosing; batch assay, PK and retail equivalence are unverified. Acute and 24-hour observations establish no chronic adaptation, productive renewal, chromosome fidelity, BUBR1 restoration or pediatric/MVA efficacy. This is a preparation-specific performance comparator, not evidence of superiority to niacin or apitegromab.
proposed_decision.identity_limit: Only exact phenylcapsaicin and source-reported aXivite names are proposed as candidates. NIH DSLD group 3951 contains both names under its source-defined Capsaicin group; this does not equate phenylcapsaicin with ordinary capsaicin or CHEMBL294199. Preserve existing capsaicin analgesia separately. No chili, food, topical preparation, analog-class, retail-product efficacy or approved-medicine equivalence follows.

exact_name_relations_summary.ordinary_capsaicin_CHEMBL294199_relation: Excluded; existing group crossrefs stay separate. Source-defined NIH grouping is not chemical equivalence.
